title: Dynamic modeling of mean-reverting spreads for statistical arbitrage

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors propose a Bayesian time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) state-space model for statistical arbitrage spreads, extending traditional pairs trading methods to accommodate time-varying parameters. The hidden state representing the spread follows a dynamic process estimated via an on-line recursive algorithm using component discount factors instead of the slow EM algorithm. The strategy models spread deviations between asset prices (or cointegrated ETFs/stocks) to monitor mean-reversion in real-time.
extraction.data_period: March 23, 1980 to August 6, 2008 (equity pairs); May 23, 2006 to August 6, 2008 (ETF pairs), daily
extraction.universe: Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Southwest Airlines (LUV); SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) and Market Vectors Gold Miners (GDX) ETFs
key_findings: Introducing time-dependent parameters via a TVAR(1) state-space model allows tracking of structural breaks and sudden losses of mean-reversion that time-invariant models miss.
An on-line Bayesian recursive algorithm using discount factors successfully recovers true model parameters and tracks mean-reversion locally without heavy computational costs.
Empirical application to XOM and LUV stock prices reveals a mean-reverting spread period from March 1980 until November 2004, after which mean-reversion is lost, consistent with cointegration tests.
Application to GLD and GDX ETFs demonstrates a valid cointegrating relationship between July 2006 and December 2007.
limitations: An empirical evaluation of actual trading strategies and transaction costs is beyond the scope of this work.
extraction.extraction_notes: The paper is methodological and theoretical regarding state-space modeling for statistical arbitrage, with illustrations on simulated and historical equity/ETF data to test cointegration and parameter tracking. It does not report trading performance figures (e.g. strategy returns, Sharpe ratios, drawdowns), so performance_metrics is correctly left empty.
